correctness.rationale: Each display H_t is the complement of one omitted x_t. An s-subset remains unseen precisely if it contains every omitted element, so U_t=C(n-K_t,s-K_t) if K_t<=s, otherwise 0, pathwise. The missing-element walk chooses one of the n-1 other vertices uniformly; when K_t=k, n-k choices are new, giving p_k=(n-k)/(n-1). Therefore K_t-1 has exactly the same finite-dimensional birth-and-hold law as ordinary iid occupancy on n-1 symbols after t-1 draws; first passage to K=s+1 equals T=1+sum_{k=1}^s independent geometric(p_k). Generating function, mean, variance and Stirling marginal laws follow exactly. If s=floor(alpha n), Riemann sums give E[T]/n=-log(1-alpha) and Var(T)/n -> 1/(1-alpha)+log(1-alpha)-1; p_k bounded away from 0 ensures Lyapunov CLT. Independent direct omission-path enumeration for n<=6, t<=5 checked all occupancy laws, exact pathwise uncollected counts, geometric mean/variance identities.
risk: The process equivalence is of scalar count finite-dimensional laws, not equality of the full sequence of omitted element identities with iid draws.
Normal limit requires 0<alpha<1 fixed; not an s=n-1 CLT.
